errorCodes.meaning: `signingKeyDid` is not the document's `issuer`, or the proof was not made by it. The enrolment must be signed by the key being enrolled — that signature is the proof of possession.
`signingKeyDid` equals `identityDid`. A delegation names a separate key; an identity already signs as itself.

The key already holds standing of its own at the consumer (for example an access-control entry). It is an identity rather than a key, and a delegation to it would take effect only once that standing was removed — turning a de-escalation into a hand-over.
The key is already enrolled — for this identity or another. Re-pointing a key at a different identity is a hand-over, not an edit; revoke it and generate a new key.
The key was enrolled and revoked. A revoked key is burned and cannot be enrolled again; generate a new one.
`expiresAt` is not in the future, so the delegation would authorize nothing.

The identity already holds as many active delegations as the consumer allows, and the enrolment names no `replaces`. Enrol again naming one of them in `replaces`, or revoke one (auth/signing-key/revoke) first. `details.maxActiveKeys` MAY state the cap. `details.activeKeys` lists the identity's active delegations so the holder can choose one to replace; a consumer MUST NOT include it unless it has accepted this enrolment's authority evidence (Conformance item 8).

The `authorization` member is not a valid auth/signing-key/authorize/0.1 document for this enrolment: its proof does not verify, it is not issued by `identityDid`, it is not addressed to this consumer, it is outside its acceptance window, its `id` was already spent, or its payload differs from this payload with `authorization` removed.

`replaces` names no active delegation of `identityDid` at this consumer. The same answer is given for a key that does not exist, is revoked or expired, or acts for a different identity, so the code reveals nothing about another identity's keys.

DeviceLabel.description: A human-readable name for where the key lives, chosen by the enrolling identity — e.g. `Work laptop — Chrome`. Read by that identity and by administrators deciding which key to revoke; retained with the delegation. Free text authored by the enrolling identity, untrusted, and attributed to it wherever it is rendered. Absent rather than invented when none was chosen: an invented label is indistinguishable from a chosen one to somebody deciding which key to revoke.

SigningKey.description: One signing-key delegation, as its holder sees it. A delegation confers nothing of its own: it names an identity that already holds whatever standing it holds, and a document signed by the key is authorized by that identity's standing read at execution time.

active.description: Whether the delegation authorizes documents right now: not revoked and not past `expiresAt`. Computed by the consumer with the predicate its verifier applies, so a holder does not re-implement it and disagree.

expiresAt.description: When the delegation stops authorizing documents. Always present: the consumer sets it at enrolment and caps it at its own maximum lifetime, whatever the producer asked for, so no delegation outlives the consumer's policy.

identityDid.description: The identity the key acts for. Included so a holder need not infer it.

lastUsedAt.description: When the delegation last authorized a document, as far as the consumer recorded. A usability signal for choosing which key to revoke, recorded best-effort; its absence does not mean the key was never used.

revokedAt.description: When the delegation was revoked. A revoked delegation authorizes nothing and its key cannot be enrolled again.

SigningKey.title: SigningKey

SigningKeyDid.description: The delegated key, as a `did:key` — an Ed25519 multikey (`z6Mk…`) derived from the public half of a keypair the holder generated for itself, typically a non-extractable browser key. `did:key` only, because its document is a function of the key and resolves with no network: a key whose DID document could be rewritten after enrolment is not the key that was enrolled.
SigningKeyDid.title: SigningKeyDid

SigningKeyScope.description: What a delegated key may be accepted for. `console`: the operations an administration console performs on the identity's behalf, authorized by the identity's own standing. Never an approver's signature on a consent or approval decision, whatever the scope: those require an `assertionMethod` key of the approver's own DID document, which a delegated key never is. A closed enumeration so a consumer cannot be asked for a scope it does not define; a later version adds values.
SigningKeyScope.title: SigningKeyScope

Free text authored by the enrolling identity, untrusted, and attributed to it wherever it is rendered. Absent rather than invented when none was chosen: an invented label is indistinguishable from a chosen one to somebody deciding which key to revoke.

schema.description: A freshly generated key asks to be enrolled as a signing-key delegation of an identity: documents it signs will be authorized by that identity's standing. The document is issued and proved by the key being enrolled, which is the proof that the enrolling party holds it; the identity it will act for is named in the payload and is established by the authority evidence the consumer requires — an operation-bound step-up, or the identity's own signed `authorization` — never by the key's own signature. Optionally replaces one of the identity's active keys in the same step. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

authorization.description: A complete, signed auth/signing-key/authorize/0.1 Trust Task document by which `identityDid` itself authorizes this enrolment: its payload is this payload with `authorization` removed. When present and valid it is the authority evidence of control over `identityDid`, in place of an operation-bound step-up. The consumer verifies it as a document in its own right — envelope, proof and payload against that specification's schemas — and over the members exactly as received: its proof covers every member, including ones this schema does not name, so it is deliberately an open object here rather than a typed one a binding could narrow.

expiresAt.description: A requested lifetime for the delegation. The consumer sets the delegation's actual expiry — no later than this, and no later than its own cap — and returns it; absent means the consumer's default lifetime. MUST be in the future when the consumer executes the task.

identityDid.description: The identity the key will act for — the DID whose standing a document signed by the key is authorized by. Naming it is not claiming it: the consumer establishes that the enrolling party controls this identity from separate authority evidence (Authorization).

replaces.description: An active delegation of the same identity to revoke in the same step as this enrolment. For a holder at the consumer's cap on active keys, whose other keys live on devices it no longer has: one authorized enrolment swaps a key out rather than needing a working key to revoke one first. Covered by the authority evidence like every other member, so evidence for adding a key cannot be reused to remove one.

schema.title: Auth — Signing Key Enroll — payload
